title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: Ten documented Emory study environments, from silent reading rooms and open science seating to reservable solo and group rooms.

cards.title: Settle In Under Matheson’s High Ceilings
cards.subtitle: A designated quiet room across the Level 3 bridge
cards.notes: Bring quiet work and use the large tables or alcove seating; voices carry easily beneath the room’s high ceilings.
cards.short_summary: A formal reading room for focused, low-noise study at long wooden tables or in upholstered alcoves.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory identifies Matheson Reading Room as a designated quiet area with large wooden tables and chairs or sofas in two alcoves.
cards.source_title: Find a Quiet Study Area | Emory Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located on Level 3 across the bridge in Candler Library; Emory requests the utmost quiet in this room. Use is subject to Woodruff Library building access and hours.

cards.entity_name: Marian K. Heilbrun Music and Media Library
cards.title: Work Beside the Wooded Views at Heilbrun
cards.subtitle: Quiet tables and media stations on Woodruff Level 4
cards.notes: Choose a large table for reading or a media station for audiovisual work while keeping conversation out of this quiet area.
cards.short_summary: A quiet library environment combining substantial tables, comfortable chairs, media stations, and woodland views.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory lists Heilbrun Music and Media Library as a designated quiet area with large wooden tables, comfortable chairs, and media viewing stations.
cards.source_title: Find a Quiet Study Area | Emory Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located on Level 4 of the Woodruff Library Building. Use is subject to library access rules and current building hours.

cards.title: Take a Computer Carrel Across from ECDS
cards.subtitle: Specialized workstations and large tables on Woodruff Level 3
cards.notes: Use a workstation carrel for computer-based assignments or spread materials across a large table; keep conversation subdued.
cards.short_summary: A quiet-leaning Level 3 workspace with individual computer carrels and larger shared work surfaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory states that the space across from the Emory Center for Digital Scholarship has individual carrels with computer workstations and large tables.
cards.source_title: Find a Quiet Study Area | Emory Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located on Level 3 across from ECDS. Loud conversation is discouraged; access follows Woodruff Library building hours and policies.

cards.title: Study in the Atwood Chemistry Atrium
cards.subtitle: An open science-library setting with individual and group seating
cards.notes: Use the atrium seating for individual work or a group session, with printing and scanning available through the branch library.
cards.short_summary: A sunlit branch-library environment inside Atwood Chemistry Center with flexible seating and practical study services.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory describes Science Commons as a branch library in the Atwood Chemistry Center atrium and depicts individual seating and group meeting spaces.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Level 2 atrium of Atwood Chemistry Center. The Science Commons page lists regular building hours as Monday–Friday, 7 a.m.–7 p.m., with weekends closed; verify exceptions before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Goizueta Business Library Group Study Spaces
cards.title: Connect the Team at Goizueta’s Study Tables
cards.subtitle: Reservable monitor-and-whiteboard tables for Goizueta students
cards.notes: Bring at least three teammates, reserve ahead, and connect a laptop to the wall monitor for shared notes or presentation review.
cards.short_summary: Two technology-equipped group tables designed for collaborative business-school assignments.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory documents two Goizueta Business Library group-study tables, each with a wall-mounted monitor and whiteboards.
cards.access_notes: Restricted to Goizueta Business School students. Reservations have a two-hour maximum and require at least three people.

cards.entity_name: MacMillan Law Library Student Study Rooms
cards.title: Reserve Uninterrupted Time at MacMillan
cards.subtitle: Ten reservable rooms for solo or group law study
cards.notes: Book up to three days ahead for uninterrupted individual or group work, keeping the daily two-hour allowance in mind.
cards.short_summary: A set of ten rooms within the law library for concentrated solo sessions or small-group collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory Law states that MacMillan Law Library has ten student study rooms available for uninterrupted solo or group study.
cards.source_title: Reserving Library Space | Emory University School of Law
cards.access_notes: Rooms are limited to law students, reservable up to three days ahead, and capped at two hours per student in each 24-hour period.

cards.entity_name: Woodruff Library Short-term Individual Study Rooms
cards.title: Close the Door for a Solo Work Block
cards.subtitle: Private reservable rooms with a desk, chair, shelves, and power
cards.notes: Reserve one for an interview, test, virtual meeting, or focused solo task; use headphones because the rooms are not soundproof.
cards.short_summary: Compact private rooms furnished for short, solitary sessions that need fewer visual and conversational distractions.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory says these one-person rooms include a desk, chair, bookshelves, and power outlet and support private short-term work.
cards.source_title: Individual Study Rooms and Carrels | Emory Libraries
cards.access_notes: Available to Emory students for one-person use. Reserve up to 14 days ahead for no more than three hours per day; rooms are private but not soundproof.

cards.title: Match the Room to the Group Project
cards.subtitle: Reservable rooms with and without technology across Woodruff
cards.notes: Check the room equipment before booking, then reserve a space suited to discussion, screen sharing, or collaborative review.
cards.short_summary: A distributed collection of enclosed group rooms offering both technology-equipped and simpler configurations.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory states that Woodruff Library has group study rooms throughout the building, including rooms with and without technology.
cards.access_notes: Advance reservation requirements and room-specific rules apply. Building maps place group study rooms on Level 4 and in the Stacks Tower.

cards.title: Find a Carrel Among the Bookstacks
cards.subtitle: Individual quiet-study seats on Stacks Tower Levels 4, 5, and 8
cards.notes: Choose an unoccupied wall carrel for individual work, stay quiet, and be ready to move if the carrel’s assigned user arrives.
cards.short_summary: Individual desks placed near the collections for quiet reading and writing with fewer group-work distractions.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory documents individual wall carrels in the bookstacks on Levels 4, 5, and 8 and permits use of vacant assigned carrels conditionally.
cards.source_title: Find a Quiet Study Area | Emory Libraries
cards.access_notes: Group conversation is discouraged. A user occupying an assigned carrel must vacate it if the assignee arrives; library access rules apply.

cards.title: Build a Tech-Ready Session at Cox Hall
cards.subtitle: Computer workstations plus reservable meeting and study rooms
cards.notes: Start at a workstation for digital assignments or reserve a room when the work calls for discussion, rehearsal, or shared screens.
cards.short_summary: A campus computing environment that supports both workstation-based individual work and reservable collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory lists computer workstations and bookable meeting or study rooms among the Computing Center at Cox Hall’s student spaces.
cards.access_notes: Room booking and center access requirements apply. Consult the Computing Center’s current schedule before visiting because operating hours and classroom availability can change.

warnings: Current hours can change for academic breaks, exams, holidays, and building exceptions; consult the linked official location pages before visiting.
Coordinates and maps URLs are null because card-level coordinates or canonical map URLs were not verified from the cited direct sources.
